title: Update on Legal Case for the Late Mr Lee Kuan Yew's Oral History Transcripts
what_it_is: Update on Legal Case for the Late Mr Lee Kuan Yew's Oral History Transcripts

sections.label: Legal proceedings on interview transcripts
sections.summary: Question asks status of executors' September 2015 suit against Government over 1983 agreement on interview transcripts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information what is the status and outcome of the legal proceedings filed by the executors of the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew's estate against the Government in September 2015 on the interpretation of an agreement in 1983 concerning the use of transcripts of interviews conducted by the Government's then Oral History Department.

sections.label: Executors file notice of appeal
sections.summary: The executors have filed a notice of appeal against the High Court's decision.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The executors have since filed a notice of appeal against the decision of the High Court.

sections.label: Parliamentary question on judgment delay
sections.summary: Member asks why judgment took long, whether rushed, and whether Judge expunged evidence at Government's request.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, Madam, the case was filed in September 2015 and, as at the time I filed my Parliamentary Question (PQ), which was in late September this year, the judgment had not yet been released.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, my question is whether the Minister is able to explain why the case took so long before the judgment came out, bearing in mind that it is an originating summons, which means that there are no witnesses coming to testify, but it is just a document interpretation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When I looked at the judgment originally released, it did contain some typographical errors in names, dates and so on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does the Government know whether the judgment was rushed out?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I understand that the Judge did not want these details to be recorded because he felt that it would be distracting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am not asking about the merits of this; I am just asking whether the Judge expunged this evidence at the application of the Government or did the Judge do this on his own accord without the Government making that request?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I read from the judgment that the family was asked to look at the transcripts at the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I will be very candid – I cannot go into the judgment, because, as the Member knows, there is an appeal before the Court of law, so we would have to leave it as that.
